(p-180) Surah al-Mujadila

It is Madani according to Ibn ʿAbbas, al-Hasan, Mujahid, ʿIkrimah, and the majority. It is reported from ʿAta' that he said: "The first ten verses of it are Madani, and the rest are Makki." And from Ibn al-Sa'ib: it is Madani except for one verse, which is His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿There is no secret conversation among three﴾.

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Allah has heard the statement of she who pleads with you concerning her husband﴾. As for the occasion of its revelation, it is reported "from ʿAʾisha, who said: Blessed is He whose hearing encompasses all voices! The woman who pleads (al-mujadila) came and spoke to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and I was in a corner of the house hearing her words, though some of them were hidden from me. She was complaining about her husband and saying: 'O Messenger of Allah, he has consumed my youth, and I have borne him children, until when my age has advanced and my childbearing has ended, he has divorced me by zihar. O Allah, I complain to You.' She said: She had not left until Jibril descended with these verses."

As for its explanation, His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Allah has heard﴾. Al-Zajjaj said: The assimilation (idgham) of the dal into the sin is good because the two articulation points are close, since both are among the letters of the tip of the tongue. Clear pronunciation of the dal is also permissible, because although it is close to the articulation point of the sin, it has its own separate place of articulation. The ta' and the ta' share the place of articulation of the dal, so these three letters have one place of articulation. The sin, the zay and the sad come from one place, and they are called the letters of whistling (huruf al-safir). Regarding the name of this woman who pleads and her lineage there are four sayings.

The first: Khawla bint Tha'laba, narrated by Mujahid from Ibn ʿAbbas; ʿIkrimah, Qatada and al-Qurazi also said this.

The second: Khawla bint Khuwaylid, narrated by ʿIkrimah from Ibn ʿAbbas.

The third: Khawla bint al-Samit, narrated by al-ʿAwfi from Ibn ʿAbbas.

The fourth: Khawla bint al-Dulayj, said by Abu al-ʿAliya. The name of her husband was Aws ibn al-Samit, and they were both from the Ansar.

Ibn ʿAbbas said: "In the Jahiliyya, when a man said to his wife, 'You are to me like the back of my mother,' she became forbidden to him. Aws was the first to make zihar in Islam. Then he regretted it and said to his wife: 'Go to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and ask him.' So she went to him, and these verses were revealed."

As for her pleading with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): whenever he said to her, "You have become forbidden to him," she would say, "By Allah, he did not mention divorce." He would say, "Nothing has been revealed to me about this," and so she kept complaining to Allah. The word tashtaki means tashku (complains). It is said: "I complained of what afflicted me" (ishtakaytu ma bi) and "I complained of it" (shakawtuhu). She said: "I have small children; if I gather them to him, they are lost, and if I gather them to myself, they go hungry." As for al-tahawur, it means the exchange of speech. ʿAntara said about his horse:

"Had it known what exchange of words means, it would have complained, and had it known speech, it would have spoken to me."

The saying of the Exalted: ﴿Those of you who liken their wives to their mothers' backs﴾. Ibn Kathir, Nafi' and Abu 'Amr read "yazzahharun" (يَظَّهَّرُونَ) with a open yā' and a doubled ẓā' and hā', both vowelled with fatḥa, and without an alif. Abu Ja'far, Ibn 'Amir, Hamza and al-Kisa'i read "yaẓẓāharūna" (يَظَّاهَرُونَ) with a open yā', a doubled ẓā', an alif, and a light hā'. 'Asim read "yuẓāhirūna" (يُظاهِرُونَ) with a ḍamma on the yā', a light ẓā' and hā', a kasra on the hā' in both places, and with the alif. Ibn Mas'ud read "yataẓāharūna" (يَتَظاهَرُونَ) with a yā', a tā' and an alif. Ubayy ibn Ka'b read "yatazahharūna" (يَتَظَهَّرُونَ) with a yā', a tā', a light yā', a doubled hā', and no alif. Al-Hasan, Qatada and al-Dahhak read "yaẓahhirūna" (يَظَهِّرُونَ) with a open yā', a open ẓā' that is light, and a hā' with a kasra that is doubled.

The meaning: they say to their wives, "You are to me like the backs of our mothers." ﴿They are not their mothers﴾. Most readers read the tā' with a kasra (ما هُنَّ أُمَّهاتِهِمْ, "mā hunna ummahātihim"). Al-Mufaḍḍal narrated from 'Asim that he read it with a ḍamma (رَفَعَها). The meaning: "The women who are made like mothers are not their mothers." ﴿Their mothers are only those who gave birth to them﴾ — that is, "their mothers are not but those who bore them."

Al-Farra' said: The accusative case of "al-ummahāt" here comes from dropping the bā' (الباء). This is the reading of 'Abdullah: "mā hunna bi-ummahātihim" (ما هُنَّ بِأُمَّهاتِهِمْ). A similar example is ﴿mā hādhā basharan﴾ [Yusuf: 31], meaning "mā hādhā bi-basharin" (this is not a human). When the bā' is dropped, its effect remains, which is the accusative. This is the speech of the people of the Hijaz. As for the people of Najd, when they drop the bā' they use the nominative, and say "mā hunna ummahātuhum" and "mā hādhā basharun." Some Arabs recited to me:

Rikabun Ḥusayl ākhira al-ṣayf budunn / wa nāqatu 'Amrin mā yuḥallu lahā raḥlu
(The mounts of Ḥusayl at the end of summer are fat, and the she-camel of 'Amr—no saddle may be placed on her.)

Wa yazʿamu Ḥaslun annahu far'u qawmihi / wa mā anta far'un yā Ḥusaylu wa lā aṣlu
(Ḥasl claims he is the branch of his people, but you are not a branch, O Ḥusayl, nor a root.)

The saying of the Exalted: ﴿And indeed they say﴾, meaning those who make zihar, ﴿an objectionable word and a falsehood﴾, because they liken wives to mothers, and mothers are forbidden permanently, unlike wives. ﴿A falsehood﴾ means a lie. ﴿Indeed Allah is Pardoning and Forgiving﴾, since He legislated expiation for this.

The saying of the Exalted: ﴿Then they return to what they said﴾. The lām in "limā" (لِما) means "ilā" (إلى). The meaning: then they return to making lawful what they had made forbidden upon themselves, namely intercourse with the wife, by resolving to have intercourse. Al-Farra' said: the meaning of the verse is that they retract what they said and undo it. Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: the meaning is that they wish to return to the intercourse which they had forbidden upon themselves. Al-Hasan, Tawus and al-Zuhri said: the "return" (al-'awd, العَوْد) is intercourse. This returns to what we have said. Al-Shafi'i said: it is that he keeps her after the zihar for a period in which he could divorce her, and does not divorce her. When this occurs, the expiation becomes binding on him, because he intended by the zihar her prohibition. If he joins that with divorce, he has followed through on what he began; if he remains silent about divorce, he has regretted what he began, so it is a return to what he was upon, and then the expiation is obligatory. Dawud said: it is repeating the utterance a second time, because the apparent meaning of the Exalted's words "yu'awwidūna" (يُعَوِّدُونَ) indicates the repetition of the utterance. Al-Zajjaj said: this is the view of one who does not know the language. Abu 'Ali al-Farisi said: it is not as they claim, because "al-'awd" may be toward something a person was not previously upon. The Hereafter is called "al-ma'ad" (the return), and no one was in it and then returned to it. Al-Hudhali said:

Wa 'āda al-fatā ka-al-kahli laysa bi-qā'ilin / siwā al-ḥaqqi shay'an wa-starāḥa al-'awādhilu
(The young man returned like a mature man, saying nothing but the truth, and the blamers have rested.)

We have explained this in the Exalted's words: ﴿And to Allah are all matters returned﴾ [al-Baqarah: 210]. Ibn Qutayba said: whoever imagines that zihar does not take effect until it is uttered a second time is mistaken, because people have agreed that zihar takes effect with one utterance. The true interpretation of the verse is that the people of the Jahiliyyah would divorce by zihar, so Allah made the ruling of zihar in Islam different from their ruling in the Jahiliyyah. He revealed the Exalted's words: ﴿And those who make zihar with their wives﴾, meaning in the Jahiliyyah, ﴿then they return to what they said﴾, meaning in Islam, that is, they return to what they used to say of this speech.

The saying of the Exalted: ﴿Then the freeing of a neck﴾. The commentators said: the meaning is: upon them, or their expiation is, the freeing of a neck, that is, its manumission. Is it required that it be a believing slave? On this there are two reports from Ahmad.

The saying of the Exalted: ﴿Before they touch one another﴾. This is a metaphor for intercourse. The scholars have disagreed on whether the one who made zihar is permitted to enjoy touching and kissing. There are two reports from Ahmad. Abu al-Hasan al-Akhfash said: the structure of the verse is: "And those who make zihar with their wives—then the freeing of a neck for what they said—then they return to their wives."

If the one who made zihar has intercourse before paying the expiation, he has sinned, and the expiation becomes established. Abu Hanifa said: the zihar and the expiation both fall away. The scholars differed about what is obligatory on him if he does this. Al-Hasan, Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, Tawus, Mujahid, Ibrahim and Ibn Sirin said: he owes one expiation. Al-Zuhri, Qatada and others said: he owes two expiations. If he says, "You are to me like my mother's back today," the zihar ends when the day passes. This is the view of our companions, Abu Hanifa, al-Thawri and al-Shafi'i. Ibn Abi Layla, Malik and al-Hasan ibn Salih said: he is a zihar-maker forever.

They differed concerning zihar with a slave-woman. Ibn 'Abbas said: there is no zihar with a slave-woman, and this was said by Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, al-Sha'bi, al-Nakha'i, Abu Hanifa and al-Shafi'i. Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Tawus, 'Ata', al-Awza'i, al-Thawri and Malik said: it is zihar. Abu Talib transmitted from Ahmad that he said: he is not a zihar-maker with respect to his slave-woman, but the expiation of zihar is binding on him, just as he said concerning a woman who makes zihar against her husband: she is not a zihar-maker, but the expiation of zihar is binding on her.

They differed about one who makes zihar repeatedly. Abu Hanifa and al-Shafi'i said: if it is in separate sessions, there are multiple expiations; if it is in one session, there is one expiation. Al-Qadi Abu Ya'la said: according to our companions, he owes one expiation whether it is in one session or in several sessions, as long as he has not paid the expiation. This is the view of Malik.

The saying of the Exalted: ﴿That is what you are admonished with﴾. Al-Zajjaj said: that severity of the expiation is what you are admonished with. The meaning: the severity of the expiation is an admonition to you, so that you abandon zihar.

We have explained this in the Exalted's words: ﴿And to Allah are all matters returned﴾ [al-Baqarah: 210]. He revealed the Exalted's words: ﴿And those who make zihar with their wives﴾, meaning in the Jahiliyyah, ﴿then they return to what they said﴾, meaning in Islam, that is, they return to what they used to say of this speech.

The saying of the Exalted: ﴿Before they touch one another﴾. This is a metaphor for intercourse. The scholars have disagreed on whether the one who made zihar is permitted to enjoy touching and kissing. There are two reports from Ahmad. Abu al-Hasan al-Akhfash said: the structure of the verse is: "And those who make zihar with their wives—then the freeing of a neck for what they said—then they return to their wives."

Section

If the one who made zihar has intercourse before paying the expiation, he has sinned, and the expiation becomes established. Abu Hanifa said: the zihar and the expiation both fall away. The scholars differed about what is obligatory on him if he does this. Al-Hasan, Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, Tawus, Mujahid, Ibrahim and Ibn Sirin said: he owes one expiation. Al-Zuhri, Qatada and others said: he owes two expiations. If he says, "You are to me like my mother's back today," the zihar ends when the day passes. This is the view of our companions, Abu Hanifa, al-Thawri and al-Shafi'i. Ibn Abi Layla, Malik and al-Hasan ibn Salih said: he is a zihar-maker forever.

They differed concerning zihar with a slave-woman. Ibn 'Abbas said: there is no zihar with a slave-woman, and this was said by Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, al-Sha'bi, al-Nakha'i, Abu Hanifa and al-Shafi'i. Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Tawus, 'Ata', al-Awza'i, al-Thawri and Malik said: it is zihar. Abu Talib transmitted from Ahmad that he said: he is not a zihar-maker with respect to his slave-woman, but the expiation of zihar is binding on him, just as he said concerning a woman who makes zihar against her husband: she is not a zihar-maker, but the expiation of zihar is binding on her.

They differed about one who makes zihar repeatedly. Abu Hanifa and al-Shafi'i said: if it is in separate sessions, there are multiple expiations; if it is in one session, there is one expiation. Al-Qadi Abu Ya'la said: according to our companions, he owes one expiation whether it is in one session or in several sessions, as long as he has not paid the expiation. This is the view of Malik.

The saying of the Exalted: ﴿That is what you are admonished with﴾. Al-Zajjaj said: that severity of the expiation is what you are admonished with. The meaning: the severity of the expiation is an admonition to you, so that you abandon zihar.

Commentary of Ibn al-Jawzi (Zad al-Masir) on surah 58, verse 8–10:

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Have you not seen those who were forbidden from secret counsel?﴾ Regarding the occasion of its revelation there are two accounts.

The first: it was revealed concerning the Jews and the hypocrites. That is because "they used to hold secret counsels among themselves, excluding the believers, and they would look at the believers and wink at one another. When the believers saw their secret counsel, they would say: 'We think they have only received news about our relatives and brothers who went out with the expeditions, that they have been killed or died or met with misfortune.' This would fall upon the hearts of the believers and grieve them, and they would continue in this state until their companions returned. When this lasted long and became frequent, the believers complained to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), so he commanded them not to hold secret counsels apart from the Muslims. They did not desist from that, so this verse was revealed." This was said by Ibn ʿAbbas.

The second: it was revealed concerning the Jews. This was said by Mujahid. Muqatil said: "There was a truce between the Jews and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). Whenever they saw a man from the Muslims alone, they would hold secret counsel among themselves, so the Muslim would suppose they were conspiring to kill him or to do something he disliked, and he would leave the road out of fear. This reached the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), so he forbade them from secret counsel, but they did not desist and returned to it, so this verse was revealed." Ibn al-Sa'ib said: it was revealed concerning the hypocrites. Al-Najwa means the act of secret counsel. ﴿Then they return﴾ to the secret counsel they were forbidden from, ﴿and hold secret counsel﴾. Hamzah, Ya'qub except Zayd and Rawh, read "wa-yatanajjaw" (with tashdid on the jim, a form of tanajjā), while the rest read "wa-yatanājaw" with an alif. Regarding the meaning of ﴿their secret counsel is of sin and aggression﴾ there are two views.

The first: they hold secret counsel about what grieves the Muslims; that is the sin and aggression, and they enjoin one another to disobey the Messenger.

The second: they hold secret counsel after the Messenger has forbidden it; that is the sin and aggression and disobedience of the Messenger.

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And when they come to you, they greet you with that by which Allah has not greeted you﴾ They differed over whom it was revealed concerning, on two accounts.

The first: it was revealed concerning the Jews. ʿA'ishah, may Allah be pleased with her, said: "Some Jews came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: 'As-sam ʿalayka, O Abu al-Qasim.' I said: 'As-sam ʿalaykum, and may Allah do to you [what He will].' The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'Mah, O ʿA'ishah, for Allah does not love obscenity or foul speech.' I said: 'O Messenger of Allah, do you not see what they say?' He said: 'Do you not see me returning to them what they say, and saying: "And upon you"?' She said: So this verse was revealed concerning that." Al-Zajjaj said: al-sam means death.

The second: it was revealed concerning the hypocrites. This was narrated by ʿAtiyyah from Ibn ʿAbbas.

The exegetes said: the meaning of ﴿they greet you﴾ is that they greeted you without the greeting of Allah upon you. They would say: "Sam ʿalayka." When they went out, they would say to themselves, or some would say to others: "If he were a prophet, we would be punished for what we say to him."

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿O you who have believed, when you hold secret counsel﴾ Regarding it there are two views.

The first: it was revealed concerning the hypocrites, and the meaning is: O you who have believed by their claim. This is the view of ʿAta' and Muqatil.

The second: it is addressed to the believers, and the meaning is that He forbade them from the deed of the hypocrites and the Jews. This is the position of a group, among them al-Zajjaj.

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿do not hold secret counsel﴾ Thus the group read it with an alif. Ya'qub alone read "fa-la tatanajjaw." As for ﴿righteousness﴾, Muqatil said it is obedience, and ﴿piety﴾ is abandoning disobedience. Abu Sulayman al-Dimashqi said: "righteousness" is truthfulness, and "piety" is abandoning lying. Then He mentioned that what the Jews and hypocrites do is from Satan, so He said, Exalted is He: ﴿Secret counsel is only from Satan﴾, that is, from his adornment; the meaning is that Satan only makes that appealing to them ﴿to grieve those who have believed﴾, and we have already explained the avoidance of what grieved the believers from this secret counsel. ﴿But it will not harm them at all﴾, that is, Satan will not harm the believers at all ﴿except by the permission of Allah﴾, that is, by His will. ﴿And upon Allah let the believers rely﴾, that is, let them entrust their affairs to Him.

[p-191] The words of the Most High, ﴿When you are told, "Make room in the gatherings"﴾. ʿĀṣim recited "fī al-majālisi" (in the gatherings) in the plural, because every sitter has a seat (majlis), so the meaning is: let each one of you make room in his seat.

The exegetes (mufassirūn) said: It was revealed concerning a group of believers who used to race to the gathering of the Messenger of God (ﷺ). When the emigrants (muhājirūn) and those of earlier precedence arrived, they found no place. The Messenger of God (ﷺ) loved that people of excellence sit near him so that they could memorize from him. One Friday, while the Messenger of God (ﷺ) was sitting in a narrow veranda (ṣuffah) in the mosque, a group of the people of Badr (ahl Badr), among them Thābit ibn Qays ibn Shammās, came. They greeted and waited for people to make room for them. Some made room for some of them, but others remained standing. This grieved the Messenger of God (ﷺ), so he said: "Stand up, so-and-so; stand up, so-and-so," until he had raised from the gathering a number of those of earlier precedence who were standing. The Messenger of God (ﷺ) saw dislike in the faces of those he had made stand. The hypocrites spoke about this and said: "By God, he has not been just." Then this verse was revealed.

Qatādah said: They used to compete for the gathering of the Messenger of God (ﷺ). When someone approached, they were stingy with their seats, so God commanded them that some of them should make room for others.

The exegetes said: The meaning of ﴿make room﴾ is "make space." That is because they used to sit crowded around the Messenger of God (ﷺ), so no one else could find a seat near him. He commanded them to make room for others, so that people would be equal in their share of him, and so that the virtue of those closest to him from the people of Badr and others would become evident.

Regarding what is meant by "al-majlis" here, there are three opinions.

The first: It is the gathering of war, the places of fighting. A man would come to a group in the battle line (al-ṣaff) and say to them, "Make room," but they would refuse him out of their eagerness for fighting. This is the view of Ibn ʿAbbās, al-Ḥasan, Abū al-ʿĀliyah, and al-Qurazī.

The second: It is the gathering of the Messenger of God (ﷺ). Mujāhid said this. Qatādah said: This was specific to the Prophet (ﷺ) and those around him.

The third: It is all gatherings of remembrance (majālis al-dhikr). This is also narrated from Qatādah. ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, Abū Razīn, Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, Mujāhid, al-Ḥasan, ʿIkrimah, Qatādah, Ibn Abī ʿAblah, and al-Aʿmash recited "tafassaḥū fī al-majālisi" with an alif, in the plural.

The words of the Most High, ﴿God will make room for you﴾, meaning: God will make room for you in Paradise and in its gatherings. ﴿And when you are told, "Rise up"﴾: Nāfiʿ, Ibn ʿĀmir, and Ḥafṣ from ʿĀṣim recited "unshuzū fa-unshuzū" with a ḍammah on the shīn. Ibn Kathīr, Abū ʿAmr, Ḥamzah, and al-Kisāʾī recited with a kasrah on the shīn in both. The meaning of "unshuzū" is "stand up." Al-Farrāʾ said: Both are dialects (lughatān). Regarding what this standing refers to, there are five opinions.

The first: It is standing up for prayer. Some men were slow to it, so they were told: When the call to prayer is made, hasten. This is the view of ʿIkrimah and al-Ḍaḥḥāk.

The second: It is standing up to fight the enemy. Al-Ḥasan said this.

The third: It is standing up to every good, whether fighting, enjoining what is right, or the like. Mujāhid said this.

The fourth: It is leaving the house of the Messenger of God (ﷺ). One: It is a report about the elevation of their ranks in Paradise. The second: It is the elevation of their seats in this world, so that their arrangement there is according to their virtues in religion and knowledge. Ibn Masʿūd used to say: O people, understand this verse and let it make you eager for knowledge, for God raises the believing scholar above those who do not know by degrees.

Commentary of Ibn al-Jawzi (Zad al-Masir) on surah 58, verse 12–13:

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿When you consult the Messenger privately﴾, there are two views regarding the occasion of its revelation.

One: "The people kept asking the Messenger of Allah ﷺ until they burdened him, so Allah wished to lighten the burden on His Prophet, and revealed this verse." This was said by Ibn ʿAbbas.

The second: it was revealed concerning the wealthy, because they used to frequently consult the Messenger of Allah ﷺ privately and would crowd out the poor from the gatherings, until the Messenger of Allah ﷺ disliked that, so this verse was revealed. As for the people of hardship, they found nothing, and as for the people of ease, they were stingy, and that weighed heavily upon the Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, so the concession was granted. This was said by Muqatil ibn Hayyan, and Muqatil ibn Sulayman went in a similar direction, except that he said: then the poor were able, at that time, to consult the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and no one from the people of ease offered charity except ʿAli ibn Abi Talib.

Mujahid narrated from ʿAli, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: "There is a verse in the Book of Allah that no one acted upon before me, and no one will act upon after me: the verse of consultation (al-Najwa). I had a dinar, so I sold it for ten dirhams, and whenever I wished to consult the Messenger of Allah ﷺ privately, I would give one dirham in charity. Then the other verse abrogated it: ﴿Are you apprehensive that you will offer charity before your private consultation?﴾ ..." to the end of the verse.

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿That is better for you and purer﴾, meaning: offering charity before the consultation is better for you, because of what it contains of obedience to Allah, and purer for your sins. ﴿But if you do not find [the means]﴾, meaning: the poor ones, ﴿then indeed Allah is Forgiving and Merciful﴾, since He pardons those who do not find [the means].

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Are you apprehensive?﴾, meaning: are you afraid of poverty through giving charity? ﴿And Allah has forgiven you﴾, meaning: He has overlooked you and lightened the obligation by abrogating the requirement of charity. Muqatil ibn Hayyan said: that lasted only ten nights. Qatadah said: it was only an hour of a day.

Commentary of Ibn al-Jawzi (Zad al-Masir) on surah 58, verse 14–19:

Allah's words: ﴿Have you not seen those who have taken as allies a people with whom Allah is angry?﴾ It was revealed concerning the hypocrites (munafiqun) who allied themselves with the Jews and passed the secrets of the believers to them. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "You did." So he went off and brought his companions, and they swore by Allah that they had not reviled him, and Allah revealed these verses.

He said: "There will come to you a man who looks at you with the eyes of a devil. When he comes to you, do not speak to him." Then a blue-eyed man came, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) called him and said: "Why do you and so-and-so and so-and-so revile me?" What follows is clear, up to His words: ﴿Those are among the most humiliated﴾, i.e., among the vanquished. For them there is humiliation in this world, and disgrace in the Hereafter.

[p-198] The words of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿God has decreed﴾, meaning God has ordained, ﴿"I shall surely prevail, I and My messengers."﴾ Nafi' and Ibn 'Amir read the *yā'* (in *لأغلبنَّ*) with a fatḥah.

The commentators (*mufassirun*) said: whoever among the messengers was sent with war, the final outcome belongs to him, and whoever was not sent with war prevails by proof (*hujjah*, argument). ﴿Indeed, Allah is Strong, Mighty﴾, meaning He protects His party from being humiliated.

The words of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿You will not find a people...﴾, the verse. The commentators differed about who it was revealed concerning, and there are four opinions.

The first: it was revealed concerning Abu 'Ubaydah ibn al-Jarrah, who killed his father on the Day of Uhud; and concerning Abu Bakr, who "called his son to single combat (*al-biraz*) on the Day of Badr, and said: 'O Messenger of Allah, let me be in the first vanguard (*al-ra'lah al-ula*).' He said: 'Let us benefit by yourself, O Abu Bakr.'" And concerning Mus'ab ibn 'Umayr, who killed his brother 'Ubayd ibn Himnah on the Day of Uhud; and concerning 'Umar, who killed his maternal uncle al-'As ibn Hisham on the Day of Badr; and concerning 'Ali and Hamzah, who killed 'Utbah and Shaybah on the Day of Badr. This was said by Ibn Mas'ud.

The second: it was revealed concerning Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, because "Abu Quhafah cursed the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), so Abu Bakr al-Siddiq struck him a severe blow that made him fall. Then he mentioned that to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to him: 'Did you actually do that?' He said: 'Yes.' He said: 'Do not return to him.' Abu Bakr said: 'By Allah, if the sword were near me, I would have killed him.' Then this verse was revealed." This was said by Ibn Jurayj.

The third: it was revealed concerning 'Abdullah ibn 'Abdullah ibn Ubayy, because "he was sitting beside the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) drank water. 'Abdullah said: 'O Messenger of Allah, leave some remainder of your drink.' He said: 'And what will you do with it?' He said: 'I will give it to my father, perhaps Allah, glory be to Him, will purify his heart.' So he did, and brought it to his father. He said: 'What is this?' He said: 'A remainder of the drink of the Messenger of Allah; I brought it to you so that you may drink it, perhaps Allah will purify your heart.'
